still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US, and exclusivity still runs to about 2031–32.
Wegovy's list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) still cost $149–150 a month cash through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not come back.
Compounding is still effectively over: the 503B exclusion (Feb 2027) is in force and 503A sales of copies remain under injunction.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Current users: 18.7% of ~268M adults ≈ 50.1M. By age: 18–29 10%×52M=5.2M; 30–49 21%×87M=18.3M; 50–64 30%×63M=18.9M; 65+ 12%×63M=7.6M; total ≈50.0M. The income thirds (24/19/13) average 18.7. Flows since 2028: of the 9.9 pts on drug in 2028, 7.0 are still on and 2.9 stopped. Of the 6.6 pts who were off in 2028, 4.0 restarted and 2.6 are still off. Of 11.5 pts of first-time starters, 7.7 are on and 3.8 have stopped. So current = 7.0+4.0+7.7 = 18.7, off-now = 2.9+2.6+3.8 = 9.3, and ever = 18.7+9.3 = 28.0. Cycled: restarters among current users = 3.5 (2028 users already on a later course) + 4.0 returners + 0.5 new starters who stopped and restarted = 8.0; restarters now off again = 2.4; (8.0+2.4)/28.0 = 37%. This growth is only possible because persistence rose from ~35% to roughly 55–65% a year in gated plans. The mechanisms are prices at $199–299, surcharge waivers tied to staying enrolled, adherence gating, and oral options with less GI trouble. Restart within a year stays at the top of the 36–47% range. Off-drug: ~24.9M adults have used and are off now, many dropped by gating cut-offs or regaining weight. ~193M have never used. The never-users skew uninsured, bottom-third, under-30, and include a growing group of young adults who refuse by choice ('unmedicated'). The 65+ rate recovered from 8% to 12% under DEXA-monitored regimens but is still below the 50–64 band. Pediatric: ~0.6% of under-18s (≈440k), mostly adolescents 12+. The oldest adolescent cohorts have about seven years of exposure, and bone-accrual data are still pending. About 3.0M users run on imported generics and are under-measured.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge extended again (Jan 2029) through Dec 2031 with the same BMI/comorbidity criteria, the same $50 copay, and the documented strength/DEXA counselling visit. Medicare's negotiated payment fell to $199/month for semaglutide and tirzepatide and $249 for retatrutide (blended ≈$210). About 3.2M beneficiaries use the Bridge for obesity: 3.2M × $210 × 12 ≈ $8.1B/yr federal. Medicare overall (Part D diabetes plus Bridge) pays 17% of incretin fills ≈ 8.5M users (≈7.6M aged 65+ plus ≈0.9M disabled under-65). Medicaid pays 9% of fills ≈ 4.5M users at ≈$205: 4.5M × $205 × 12 ≈ $11.1B/yr combined, ≈$7.2B of it federal at a ~65% blended match. Six states (Indiana, Arkansas, Ohio, Tennessee, Georgia, Utah) run adherence-and-weigh-in 1115 waivers.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 80+ generic semaglutide brands at $6–40/month, with generic oral semaglutide common. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 60–90. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey, China and the Gulf all have local generics. Generic liraglutide is global. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: TrumpRx and manufacturer-direct cash prices are semaglutide injectable $199, tirzepatide $249, retatrutide $299 (TrumpRx since Jan 2030, when allocation ended), and orals $149 starting / $199 maintenance. List prices are unchanged (Wegovy $1,349, retatrutide $1,499) and mostly fictional. Lilly and Novo agreed to the cuts as part of Section 232 tariff relief tied to US plant commitments. Payer mix of ≈50.0M users: commercial 46% (23.0M), Medicare 17% (8.5M), Medicaid 9% (4.5M), cash/direct 22% (11.0M), gray/imported 6% (3.0M) = 100%. Cash/direct includes ≈4M off-label 'craving', cessation and longevity users on low-dose orals through telehealth. The largest branded-oral 'calm' subscription service has ≈1.2M subscribers. Who pays is structurally unchanged, but what employers require has changed: ~55% of covering employers now run adherence-gated PBM programmes, up from ~40%. Under 2029 tri-agency guidance, staying enrolled with ≥80% proportion of days covered counts as meeting a BMI-linked wellness standard, which waives surcharges of up to 30% of premium. Commercial users doubled mostly inside already-covering employers, as employees enrolled to escape the surcharge. Semaglutide's 2029 smoking-cessation approval brought it under existing ACA preventive coverage of FDA-approved cessation drugs (two 90-day courses a year), which created a second commercial on-ramp.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide; unallocated since Nov 2029)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
Glucagon/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Feb 2029, positioned on MASH and weight)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Nov 2029, limited launch)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: smoking cessation as adjunct to standard therapy (semaglutide, approved Apr 2029)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: gambling disorder: phase 3 positive (Mar 2030), orforglipron sNDA under priority review with a decision due ~Q1 2031; widely prescribed off-label now, and paid for by problem-gambling funds in New Jersey, Ohio and Massachusetts
'compulsion' and 'craving' use (shopping, scrolling, porn, sports betting) via telehealth subscriptions selling low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo
'metabolic health' / longevity use by people without obesity, still mostly the top income third
pediatric under-12 use off-label under specialist care
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The triple-agonist driver is met by retatrutide. It was approved in Mar 2028; in this window it went from allocated supply to general availability (Nov 2029, after new plants in North Carolina and Indiana) and got a $299 TrumpRx price (Jan 2030). That turned surgical-grade loss (28% at 80 weeks, ~30% at BMI≥35) into a mass-market pen. Survodutide (filed Oct 2027) was approved Feb 2029. Amycretin (filed Jun 2028) was approved Nov 2029 and launched with limited supply. MariTide (monthly) has not filed and is not on the market, with a filing expected 2031. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) are in phase 3 and not approved. The compulsion indication is met by a filing: the orforglipron gambling-disorder sNDA (filed Apr 2030, priority review), and no compulsion indication is approved by the end of 2030. The incretin market is ≈$135B in 2030: US volume nearly doubled at ~20% lower net prices, partly offset by ex-US generic erosion.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common class effect and the leading cause of voluntary discontinuation. Lower on low-dose orals and higher with retatrutide escalation.
Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute event counts are rising with broad retatrutide use.
No causal confirmation in longer data; absolute risk low.
Unchanged finding: ~1.5× sarcopenia criteria in 65+ users on therapy >2 years; lean share of loss ~25–40%. Real-world retatrutide data match the label.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 2028 class label stands. Medicare Bridge renewal still requires a counselling visit. No new action.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fracture HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term users, concentrated in women and repeat cyclers. No new data changed the estimate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class BMD labelling and DEXA recommendation stand. The Senate HELP report (2029) criticised Novo's disclosure. Novo resolved the DOJ civil investigation with a settlement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Unchanged: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Survey estimates still ~10–15% of long-term users report reduced pleasure, dose-dependent. First interim anhedonia-scale data from retatrutide postmarketing are inconclusive. The effect is now being marketed outright as a benefit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. FDA warning letters (2029–30) to telehealth sellers for unapproved 'calm/focus' claims, but none about harm.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year. Involuntary stops from gating cut-offs now affect hundreds of thousands a year across six Medicaid waivers and gated employer plans.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: District court upheld Indiana's waiver (2029); appeal pending in the 7th Circuit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Continued observational signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now exist. Adolescent bone-accrual studies are enrolling but have not reported.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; pediatric bone-accrual studies ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mostly imported and counterfeit pens. Poison-centre calls are roughly flat as legitimate prices fell.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts and selective parcel seizures; individuals still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent of users; usually transient.

food_and_beverage.state: With nearly one adult in five on drug, volume pressure on snacks, confectionery, sugary drinks and frozen meals is clearly steeper than in 2026–28, about 3–5% annual unit declines in high-uptake categories. Portfolios keep shifting to protein, fibre and smaller packs. A counter-trend serves the young 'unmedicated' cohort: high-calorie 'honest food' brands and bulking products grow from a small base.

alcohol.state: Volumes are down again, with heavy drinkers concentrated among users, EAP referrals continuing, and cessation-indication users added. Spirits majors restructure US distribution. Craft breweries close faster than they open. Non-alc and 'one good drink' premium hold up.

restaurants.state: Traffic is roughly flat and checks are smaller. Half-portions, protein-by-the-gram and shared plates are universal. 'Feast' supper clubs and steakhouses aimed at the unmedicated young do well in Brooklyn, Austin and LA. Buffets and value-volume chains in high-uptake suburbs keep closing.

apparel.state: Size runs keep widening in both directions. Plus-size is stable. Menswear sees demand for cuts built for visible muscle (shoulders, thighs), part of the move away from thinness as the ideal.

fitness.state: Growing on two engines: prescribed strength training for users (DEXA-plus-coaching chains, Medicare Advantage strength benefits) and 'unmedicated' strength culture among under-35s. Natural bodybuilding and powerlifting federations add GLP-1 agonists to banned-substance lists and test for them.

insurance.state: No change in who pays. Employer coverage is ~57%, but use doubled inside covering plans because surcharge waivers reward staying on. Unit prices are lower, yet incretins are now ~15% of commercial pharmacy spend and premiums rose ~8% a year. Gating, PDC dashboards and outcomes contracts are standard.

pharma.state: Market ≈$135B. Lilly leads with retatrutide and Foundayo, but its 2030 False Claims Act settlement over telehealth promotion and its corporate integrity agreement constrain marketing. Novo stabilised under new management. Boehringer (survodutide) and Novo (amycretin) take share at the margin. Sportsbook operators and tobacco firms list incretins as a risk factor.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness is cheap and so no longer signals much. Among insured over-40s a lean body reads as 'enrolled', the way braces once signalled dental insurance. The newly scarce body has visible muscle, eats with open appetite, and is plausibly unmedicated. It signals time, coaching, food budget, and freedom from the surcharge-and-gating system.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use is now widest in the middle (19%) and still highest in the top third (24%), but the meaning has flipped at the top among the young. Brooklyn and Los Angeles creatives aged 25–34 call themselves 'unmedicated' as a status claim. Affluent 50-somethings stay on low-dose regimens with DEXA and strength coaching, while mid-income workers stay on to avoid premium surcharges. Bottom-third users cycle with Medicaid gating or buy Indian pens. In Dallas–Fort Worth insurance offices, about half of women aged 45–60 are on a drug, and their adult children work at lifting gyms advertising 'unmedicated coaches'.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Two food cultures sit at one table: grazers on the drug and eaters off it. Among the young off-drug, a big shared meal has become a kind of performance. 'Feast nights' and eating in public on camera signal that you are not on anything.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added 'unmedicated' as a profile tag, and it is the most-searched filter among users under 30. Claims are unverifiable, and accusations of 'secret dosing' are a running joke and occasional grievance. Mismatched appetite between on and off partners is a standard couples-therapy topic.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has split in meaning. For the insured middle-aged it is still a risk to be managed. For the young and the wealthy it has become the scarce good, read as vitality and proof of an unmedicated self. Both readings coexist in the same families.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Surveys still put reduced pleasure at ~10–15% of long-term users, with no RCT-grade measure. The effect is now sold on purpose. Telehealth 'calm' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo at $149–199 cash) are prescribed off-label for craving, shopping, scrolling and betting, with ≈1.2M subscribers at the largest service. Employers still reward the correlates: fewer sick days, lower EAP claims, steadier reviews.
interior_life.framing: Sold as 'quiet', 'craving-free' and 'focus'. The marketing avoids weight entirely. Users who dislike it call it 'the flat'. Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. Gambling-treatment counsellors call it a treatment, and FDA warning letters call the claims unapproved.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Knowledge-work managers informally recommend 'quiet' subscriptions to staff with focus or phone-habit problems. Some firms reimburse them through lifestyle spending accounts, which sidesteps pharmacy-benefit rules. Gating dashboards still link refills to the surcharge. Sales, trading and creative roles drift off-dose or say they do. Logistics, compliance and call-centre roles stay on.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' work is a selling point: albums and stand-up specials advertise being made unmedicated. Sports-betting handle growth slows in high-uptake states. Mobile-game studios report lower spending among whales and redesign monetisation around novelty rather than compulsion.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Reduced-desire reports persist. 'Quiet' subscriptions marketed against porn compulsion add a new group of partners on low doses. Sex therapists ask about dose, timing and whether the prescription came from a telehealth 'calm' service.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Fights over cost and control now include a fight over identity. 'Unmedicated' is claimed by MAHA-aligned influencers on the right and anti-surveillance activists on the left, even as the administration promotes TrumpRx price cuts. Unions bargain over surcharge waivers and PBM data. Sportsbooks lobby against state funds paying for off-label gambling prescriptions. No measurable change in turnout is established.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on approvals and prices (survodutide, amycretin, the cessation indication, retatrutide price deal). Enforcement focuses on marketing rather than safety: FCA settlement with Lilly, warning letters to 'calm' telehealth sellers. No new safety action, since no new signal emerged. Import enforcement is still selective.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Bridge runs through 2031 at $199/$249 with a $50 copay. TrumpRx prices are $199–299 for injectables and $149–199 for orals. ACA preventive coverage applies to semaglutide for cessation. Medicaid is state by state.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Benefits conditioning has spread. Six Medicaid 1115 waivers (IN, AR, OH, TN, GA, UT) require ≥80% PDC plus quarterly verified weigh-ins; miss two checks and coverage ends for 12 months. Under 2029 tri-agency wellness guidance, continuous enrolment in a 'metabolic programme' satisfies BMI-linked standards that would otherwise carry surcharges of up to 30% of premium. That turns refill data into a premium input for tens of millions. The Indiana waiver was upheld at district level, with the appeal pending.
state.workforce_or_military: The DOT sleep-apnea route keeps tirzepatide a de facto requirement for many drivers. The Army allows use for recruits who meet standards. Some state corrections and police departments pilot 'craving' prescriptions in employee assistance.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariff relief was traded for US plant commitments and price step-downs. India's generic mail exports (~3M US users) remain a trade irritant. Retatrutide is now produced domestically at scale.

events.event: CMS extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2031 and cuts its payment to $199/month (copay stays $50); Lilly and Novo, granted Section 232 tariff relief for US plant commitments, drop TrumpRx injectable prices to $199–249 and oral maintenance to $199

Labor, HHS and Treasury issue wellness guidance letting employers treat continuous enrolment with ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered in a 'metabolic programme' as meeting BMI-linked standards; Ohio, Tennessee, Georgia and Utah win Medicaid waivers modelled on Indiana's, and a federal judge upholds Indiana's

Telehealth firms launch 'calm' subscriptions selling low-dose oral semaglutide and Foundayo off-label for craving, shopping and betting, marketed without reference to weight; FDA sends warning letters over 'focus' claims as subscriber counts pass one million
Lilly ends retatrutide allocation as new North Carolina and Indiana capacity comes online and announces a $299 TrumpRx price from January; prescriptions roughly triple within two quarters

Phase 3 trial shows orforglipron reduces gambling-disorder severity versus placebo; Lilly files for the indication under priority review while New Jersey, Ohio and Massachusetts problem-gambling funds begin paying for off-label prescriptions

Lilly agrees to pay $1.9B, without admitting wrongdoing, to resolve DOJ False Claims Act allegations that it paid telehealth partners to steer 'calm' and craving patients to Foundayo through scripted intake, including Medicaid-billed off-label fills; it accepts a five-year corporate integrity agreement

open_tensions: Refill data now set premiums for tens of millions and decide Medicaid coverage in six states, rewarding continuous long-term exposure that the label still warns weakens older bones. The 7th Circuit appeal will decide whether abrupt cut-offs are lawful.

The reward-blunting mechanism is sold as 'quiet', reimbursed as focus and filed as a gambling treatment, yet it is still unmeasured as a harm. The orforglipron decision in 2031 will either legitimise or constrain the whole 'calm' market.

As thinness becomes the cheap, enrolled body, the young and affluent reject it for an unmedicated, muscular, hungry ideal. That puts an employer-and-state system built to keep people on the drug in conflict with a culture that increasingly prizes being off it.

Brand prices have stepped down to $199–299, but US exclusivity ends in 2031–32 against $6–40 Indian generics already used by ~3M Americans, and nobody has settled whether the import channel will be legalised, ignored or shut.

prose.headline: Fifty Million on the Pen: Thin Is Cheap Now, and the Body Everyone Wants Is the One That Still Gets Hungry
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030, nearly one American adult in five is on an incretin drug, about fifty million people, double the number two years ago. The bone scandal and its fallout have not gone away. The increase has prosaic causes: prices came down, and benefits paperwork rewards staying on.

Prices came down in negotiated steps rather than all at once. In January 2029 Lilly and Novo got relief from the Section 232 pharmaceutical tariffs in exchange for building plants in the United States, and in return they cut TrumpRx prices. Semaglutide now costs $199 a month cash, tirzepatide $249, and oral maintenance doses $199. Medicare cut its own payment to $199 and extended its Bridge programme to 2031, with the $50 copay unchanged. List prices stayed where they were, and nobody pays them. Retatrutide, the triple agonist that produces surgical-grade weight loss from a weekly pen, was rationed until new plants opened in late 2029. It is now on TrumpRx at $299, and its prescriptions tripled within two quarters.

The paperwork matters more than the price. A 2029 federal guidance let employers count continuous enrolment in a 'metabolic programme' as meeting the weight standards behind wellness surcharges, which can reach 30 percent of a premium. Staying on the drug became the cheapest way to keep your health plan affordable, so people at companies that already covered the drugs enrolled in large numbers. More than half of those employers now check refills through pharmacy-benefit dashboards. Six states run Medicaid the way Indiana does: a quarterly weigh-in at a kiosk scale, refill adherence above 80 percent, and a year-long cutoff for anyone who slips twice. A federal judge upheld Indiana's rules, and the appeal is pending. Who pays has not changed; what payers watch has.

There is no new safety signal, and the old warnings remain on the label. Older users came back carefully, with DEXA scans and prescribed lifting. The FDA has spent this window on marketing problems rather than medical ones. In 2029 telehealth companies began selling low-dose oral pills as 'quiet', meaning freedom from craving. They are pitched against betting apps, online shopping and endless scrolling, and weight is never mentioned. More than a million people subscribe to the largest service, and some employers reimburse it out of lifestyle accounts. In July Lilly paid $1.9 billion, without admitting wrongdoing, to settle claims that it paid telehealth partners to steer these patients to its pill. Months earlier its gambling-disorder trial had succeeded, and the FDA will rule on that indication in 2031. Problem-gambling funds in New Jersey and Ohio already pay for off-label prescriptions, and the sportsbooks are lobbying against them.

Meanwhile thinness has stopped meaning much. In insurance offices in Dallas–Fort Worth, about half of women between forty-five and sixty are on a drug, and their leanness reads as 'enrolled'. Their children, especially creative workers in their late twenties in Brooklyn and Los Angeles, want the opposite: visible muscle, a big appetite eaten in public, and the word 'unmedicated' on a dating profile, where it is now the most-searched tag among users under thirty. Natural bodybuilding federations test for GLP-1s. Steakhouses and 'feast' supper clubs do well while snack volumes fall. MAHA influencers on the right and privacy activists on the left both claim the unmedicated body, even as the administration takes credit for cheaper pens.

On the surface the country looks healthy and calm. Drinking is down, betting growth has slowed, and sick days have fallen. Underneath, refill data sets premiums, the drug's quieting effect on craving is sold without having been measured as a harm, and the generation that will inherit a cheap generic in 2032 is deciding that being hungry is what makes someone worth looking at.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Treviño weighs in at 7:10, before her shift, on the kiosk scale at the CVS off MacArthur Boulevard in Irving. The receipt prints a QR code. She photographs it for the benefits portal anyway, because last spring the upload failed and HR emailed about her surcharge.

At the claims floor, the woman in the next cubicle is on retatrutide now that it's $299. She brings a pouch of shredded chicken and eats half. Marisol is on Zepbound, $25 copay, day four of the week. She isn't hungry. She is rarely hungry.

At noon her husband Rubén texts a screenshot: forty-one days without a bet. His pill comes in a matte white box from a telehealth company that says QUIET on the lid, $149 a month on his own card. He says Sundays are boring now. He says it like it's good news.

After work she drives to the gym in Deep Ellum where her daughter Ana coaches. A banner over the racks reads ALL COACHES UNMEDICATED. Ana is deadlifting something enormous, shoulders like a swimmer's. She finishes and eats a burrito in six bites, laughing, sauce on her wrist.

'You want some, Mamá?'

Marisol takes a bite to be polite. It is good. She can tell it is good. She hands it back.

In the car she checks the portal. Adherence: 96%. Status: compliant. Premium: standard.

At home Rubén is watching the Rangers with the sound off, not checking his phone, perfectly still.

least_plausible_claims.quote: This growth is only possible because persistence rose from ~35% to roughly 55–65% a year in gated plans.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails magnitude: the same note's flows have 7.0 of 9.9 pts (71%) of 2028 users still on after two years and 7.7 of 11.5 new starters (67%) on. That cannot come from 55–65% annual persistence without a restart story the note never gives.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Semaglutide's 2029 smoking-cessation approval brought it under existing ACA preventive coverage of FDA-approved cessation drugs (two 90-day courses a year), which created a second commercial on-ramp.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism and magnitude: preventive-coverage mandates attach through USPSTF recommendations, not automatically through FDA approval. The Apr 2029 approval is also only ~11 months after the May 2028 filing, inside the envelope's 12-month floor. The 'second on-ramp' is asserted, not shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: orforglipron sNDA under priority review with a decision due ~Q1 2031
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism: the events list the filing in Mar 2030 while the pipeline note says Apr 2030. A priority-review sNDA filed then would be decided around Oct 2030, not Q1 2031. A phase 3 for a use that was only 'anecdotal' in 2028 is also very fast.

rationale.badness: About 50M adults are on drug, and refill data now set premiums for tens of millions (the 2029 wellness guidance). Six Medicaid waivers cut coverage after missed weigh-ins, and the 'calm' subscription market sells reward blunting that is still unmeasured as a harm. Prices fell, so access widened. The harm is structural and normalised: autonomy and epistemic clarity suffer most, and the family and generational split over 'unmedicated' is a cohesion cost. That puts it above a harder 2028 but below a society people would refuse to live in.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable in events and fields: managed-decline prices ($199–299), benefits conditioning, retatrutide general availability, the Lilly scandal, the 'calm' marketed feature, aesthetic inversion, and compulsion realised as a sNDA filing. Safety_signal 'none' is honoured. Coverage_shift 'status_quo' is slightly strained by the ACA cessation on-ramp and the waiver spread (claim 2). mechanism: The surcharge-waiver chain explaining commercial users doubling is well shown. The persistence jump (claim 1), the ACA coverage leap (claim 2) and the sNDA timing (claim 3) are asserted or inconsistent. The 65+ rebound from 8% to 12% despite the fracture signal is only thinly justified. magnitude: The headline figures sit inside the envelope (18.7%, 28%, income thirds, survodutide and amycretin approval timing). Payer shares, Medicare/Medicaid dollar arithmetic and the cycling arithmetic reconcile. Gaps are the flows implying ~70% two-year retention against the stated 55–65% annual persistence, and the cessation approval about one month under the 12-month floor from the May 2028 filing.
rationale.generativity: Marisol, Rubén and Ana are distinct, and the Irving kiosk weigh-in, the QR receipt, the QUIET lid and the unmedicated gym banner are concrete scenes. The details are fully usable: Rubén's flat Sundays, Marisol finding the burrito good without wanting it, and the 96% adherence portal. Each section of the world state (dating tags, feast clubs, union bargaining, sportsbook lobbying) opens further scenes.

least_plausible_claims.quote: This growth is only possible because persistence rose from ~35% to roughly 55–65% a year in gated plans.
least_plausible_claims.why: The note's own flows have 7.0 of 9.9 pts still on after two years (~71%) and 7.7 of 11.5 new starters still on (~67%). That implies annual persistence near 80%+, not 55–65%, and a 61% restart rate among those off in 2028, so the reconciliation fails (magnitude) and the stated mechanism does not match its own arithmetic.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Sports-betting handle growth slows in high-uptake states. Mobile-game studios report lower spending among whales and redesign monetisation around novelty rather than compulsion.
least_plausible_claims.why: The stated base is ~4M off-label craving users and 1.2M 'calm' subscribers, and the 'calm' services launched only in Aug 2029. Measurable macro effects on betting handle and game-studio monetisation within about a year are asserted with no chain from those numbers (mechanism and magnitude).

least_plausible_claims.quote: Commercial users doubled mostly inside already-covering employers, as employees enrolled to escape the surcharge.
least_plausible_claims.why: BMI-linked surcharges of up to 30% already existed in 2028, when persistence and starts were low. A $50–100 cash price cut and one 2029 waiver rule are shown as the cause of ~11M extra commercial users and 11.5 pts of first-time starters. Most people facing a BMI-linked surcharge already qualified, so the chain is thin and the effect is asserted.

rationale.badness: Refill data now sets premiums for tens of millions and decides Medicaid coverage in six states, so continuous exposure is rewarded despite the unchanged bone and sarcopenia findings. 'Calm' subscriptions sell reward blunting as a feature while its harm remains unmeasured (epistemic 7). Cheaper access, 65+ use recovering under DEXA monitoring, and the lack of new safety signals keep flourishing and inequality from rising higher. The worsening is mostly structural coercion and cultural splitting, not acute harm.
